advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reduce _peak_rolling_hour to incremental/amortized counting (or memoize _distinct_file_impact_ticket per ticket_id) to avoid O(n^2) recomputation and repeated disk I/O in the duplicate metric.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:384-388: loop over `end` recomputes `count(events[start:end+1])` each iteration
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:417: duplicate metric passes `lambda window: _duplicate_excess(repo_root, window)` as the count
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:372-373: `_distinct_file_impact_ticket(repo_root, event.get('_ticket_id')) for event in matches` inside _duplicate_excess re-reads FILE_IMPACT files
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:336-339: _distinct_file_impact_ticket calls _event_files (os.listdir) + _load per ticket
`for end, event in enumerate(events): ... peak = max(peak, count(events[start : end + 1]))` (lines 384-388) — one `count(window)` call per event
`_peak_rolling_hour(events, lambda window: _duplicate_excess(repo_root, window))` (line 417) — count is O(window), giving O(N^2)
`_duplicate_excess` iterates the full window: `for event in events: ... grouped.setdefault(title_norm, []).append(event)` (lines 361-366)
`_create_events` returns every in-range CREATE with no size cap: `events.append(event)` inside nested dir/file loops (lines 318-323)
advisory.finding: `_peak_rolling_hour` recomputes the `count` callable over a fresh slice `events[start:end+1]` for every event (O(n^2)); for `duplicate_title_peak_hour` the count callable is `_duplicate_excess`, which re-runs `normalize_title` grouping AND `_distinct_file_impact_ticket` (which does per-ticket `os.listdir`/`_load` disk I/O) for every event in every window, giving O(n^2) filesystem reads.
merged_from: `duplicate_title_peak_hour` is O(N^2) in the number of in-range CREATE events: `_peak_rolling_hour` invokes `_duplicate_excess` once per event, and each `_duplicate_excess` call rescans the whole rolling-hour window. The event count is data/rate-controlled (all CREATEs in the query range), and the metric is designed to fire during creation surges — the exact condition that maximizes N.
scenarios: A busy period with hundreds/thousands of CREATE events in the range (e.g. the very mass-creation surge this metric is meant to detect)
advisory.suggested_fix: Cache `_distinct_file_impact_ticket` results by ticket_id, and/or maintain an incremental sliding-window count rather than recomputing over the full slice each step.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document whether empty-normalized-title creates should be exempt from the duplicate-title alarm, or group them under a sentinel key so they are still counted.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:364-366: `title_norm = normalize_title(...)` then `if title_norm: grouped.setdefault(...)`
src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:57: normalize_title returns '' for whitespace/punctuation-only input
advisory.finding: CREATE events whose title normalizes to the empty string are silently dropped from duplicate grouping (`if title_norm:`), so an operator flooding many creates with blank/punctuation-only titles would never trip the duplicate-title alarm.
scenarios: Bulk creates with empty or punctuation-only titles

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with multiple CREATEs authored by `rebar-bridge[bot]` titled `[binding-drift] ...` asserting they are exempt (contribute no duplicate excess).
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:355-356 `return event.get("author") == "rebar-bridge[bot]" and title.startswith("[binding-drift]")`
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:362-363 `if _recurring_alert_create(event): continue`
search of tests for `binding-drift` shows only canary/bridge tests, none in the metrics suite; test _write_event hardcodes author 't'

Named violating input: several CREATEs with author `rebar-bridge[bot]` and title `[binding-drift] ...` should contribute 0 excess; a regression that dropped the exemption would over-count these as duplicates undetected.
advisory.finding: The _recurring_alert_create exemption for bridge fsck alerts is untested. No test creates a CREATE authored by `rebar-bridge[bot]` with a `[binding-drift]` title, so the exemption branch that skips these events in _duplicate_excess never runs.
scenarios: The bridge-alert exemption is removed or its author/title match drifts, causing recurring bridge alerts to trip the duplicate-title alarm.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Memoize `_distinct_file_impact_ticket` per (repo_root, ticket_id) so FILE_IMPACT files are read once, not per overlapping window.
evidence: `impacts = { _distinct_file_impact_ticket(repo_root, event.get("_ticket_id")) for event in matches }` (lines 372-374) — called per duplicate event per window
`_distinct_file_impact_ticket` reads disk each call: `impact_events = _event_files(ticket_dir, "FILE_IMPACT", ...)` then `_load(impact_events[-1])` (lines 336-339)
`_event_files` does `os.listdir(ticket_dir)` per call (line 87); `_load` opens+parses JSON (lines 99-100)
No memoization: `_distinct_file_impact_ticket` has no cache and is invoked from inside the O(N) `_peak_rolling_hour` loop
advisory.finding: `_duplicate_excess` performs filesystem I/O (`os.listdir` + `json.load`) via `_distinct_file_impact_ticket` for each duplicate-title event, and this is re-executed for the same ticket across every overlapping rolling-hour window with no caching, producing quadratic disk reads.
scenarios: Many same-normalized-title CREATEs in a range cause repeated FILE_IMPACT file reads for the same tickets across each overlapping window
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute each ticket's distinct-file-impact discriminator once up front (or via an lru_cache keyed on ticket_id) before the rolling-hour scan, so the nested window loop never re-reads the same FILE_IMPACT files from disk.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the peak-hour metrics emit an explicit measured zero (e.g. `_alarm_value(0, threshold)`) on empty-but-healthy input so 'no creates' is distinguishable from 'observer down', matching the docstring.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:409 docstring: "Missing data is not breaching: this observer publishes measured zeroes; absent output means the observer itself is down."
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:413-415: `events = _create_events(...)` then `if not events: return None`

A quiet-but-healthy hour (no creates) yields None, the same sentinel a downed/never-run observer would produce; the consumer cannot distinguish 'measured zero' from 'observer down', so the alarm fails open.
blocking.finding: `duplicate_title_peak_hour`/`create_volume_peak_hour` return None when there are simply zero CREATE events in the range (`if not events: return None`), which is indistinguishable from the observer never having run — directly contradicting the docstring's own claim that this observer 'publishes measured zeroes; absent output means the observer itself is down.'
scenarios: A range window with legitimately zero CREATE events
Observer misconfigured / tracker dir missing so _create_events returns []
blocking.suggested_fix: Return `_alarm_value(0, _DUPLICATE_TITLE_ALARM_THRESHOLD)` / `_alarm_value(0, _CREATE_VOLUME_ALARM_THRESHOLD)` when `not events`, instead of None, so absence uniquely signals observer-down.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a duplicate_title_peak_hour test with two same-title CREATEs each carrying a distinct single-file FILE_IMPACT, asserting the pair is suppressed (peak_hour reflects 0 excess).
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:372-376 `impacts = { _distinct_file_impact_ticket(...) for event in matches }; if None not in impacts and len(impacts) == len(matches): continue`
search of tests/unit/metrics for `FILE_IMPACT` returned (no matches)

Named violating input: two same-normalized-title CREATE tickets, each with one FILE_IMPACT event listing a distinct single file path, should yield excess 0 (suppressed) — a regression that broke the suppression (e.g. inverting the condition) would go undetected.
blocking.finding: The _distinct_file_impact_ticket suppression path (which prevents legitimate same-title, distinct-single-file work from counting as duplicate excess) is entirely untested. No test writes any FILE_IMPACT event, so none of the discriminator's branches (single-file str impact, dict impact via path/file key, len!=1 fallthrough) or the suppression condition `None not in impacts and len(impacts) == len(matches)` ever executes.
scenarios: A refactor or logic change breaks the distinct-file-impact suppression and legitimate path-collision work starts false-alarming.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a duplicate_title_peak_hour test that packs >11 same-normalized-title CREATEs into one rolling hour and asserts alarm=True.
evidence: tests/unit/metrics/test_event_metrics.py:103 asserts `{"peak_hour": 1, "alarm_threshold": 10, "alarm": False}` — only the below-threshold case
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:392-397 `_alarm_value` sets `alarm: peak_hour > threshold`

Named violating input: 12 same-normalized-title CREATEs within one hour should give excess 11 and alarm=True; no test drives excess above 10 for the duplicate metric, so a threshold/comparison regression on that path is undetected.
blocking.finding: The alarm-true path of duplicate_title_peak_hour (peak_hour > _DUPLICATE_TITLE_ALARM_THRESHOLD of 10, giving alarm=True) is never exercised. The sole duplicate-title test asserts peak_hour=1/alarm=False, mirroring only the volume metric's alarm coverage; the duplicate metric's threshold-crossing branch is untested.
scenarios: A regression in _duplicate_excess accumulation or the threshold comparison for the duplicate metric fails to raise alarm on a genuine title-duplication surge.
